rust.note: 35 failures are the pre-existing macOS run of Windows-only path/PATH tests; the failed-test name list is byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (`comm -23` and `comm -13` against /tmp/baseline_failures.txt are both empty)

browser.note: Three consecutive full-suite runs of 81 passed. Two test-side defects were fixed on the way: the status mock did not answer the new `status_pages` command, and `prompt cache countdown` raced its own fake clock (`install({time: T})` then `pauseAt(T)` throws "Cannot fast-forward to the past" once a millisecond has passed; it failed on pristine specs too, about one full-suite run in three).

windows.note: First Windows run of the suite, on the GitHub Actions windows-latest runner (.github/workflows/windows-check.yml, run 39440841593 at 8e7f6f5). The 35 tests that fail on macOS because they exercise Windows paths and PATH pass here, so this is a stricter bar than the macOS baseline. It found two real defects macOS could not compile or observe (a missing PathBuf import in the Windows-only system_path, and a path-as-identity comparison that gave one transcript two names by separator) plus three tests that assumed a POSIX host; all are fixed in their own commits. It does not build installers: the build step is --no-bundle.
windows.releaseBuild: The same run that published also ran the full suites before bundling: 1212 Rust passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored; 260 frontend passed; tsc --noEmit clean.

frontendWindows.note: vitest and tsc --noEmit both ran on the Windows runner, not only on macOS.

implementedVerified: All 54 Pulse 1.9 Token sources registered with a fixture-backed reader each; Warp and Freebuff report no token counts by the original's own design and say so instead of estimating
Window starter: per-provider opt-in with a risk confirmation, shared local hours, reset-plus-grace scheduling, first-account-only rule, one attempt per reset, recorded outcome

User extensions: manifest scan with schema/id/executable-path validation, off by default, per-extension switch, 1-60 s timeout, output ceiling and JSON validation, failure classification, one account per extension in the panel, metrics drawn on the card and in Settings

Official service status: 45-entry catalogue (44 providers plus the second MiniMax storefront) over 12 feed shapes, the original's five-rule component matching, 7 palettes, one request per feed for outage notifications, OutageMemory keyed by provider id
Currency: 7 display currencies, estimates only (a service's own balance/credits/console charge stays in its own currency), network only when the chosen currency is not USD, manual rate overrides
Token spend spans: all 9 of the original's, including custom start/end days, with the one-day range switching to the hour profile

Hide from screen capture: `capture::protected` via Tauri's `set_content_protected`, which tao maps to `SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE)` on Windows and to the original's `NSWindow.sharingType` on macOS

publicVerification.signatureCryptography: Ed25519 verification of each installer against the pinned public key over the BLAKE2b-512 prehash (minisign's ED scheme) passed for both the nsis setup and the msi.
publicVerification.updaterEndpoint: https://github.com/wapearoudy/PulseWin/releases/latest/download/latest.json returns 200 with version 0.1.18 and three platforms, so the endpoint every installed client reads resolves.
publicVerification.latestRelease: The GitHub API reports v0.1.18 as the latest release, not a draft and not a prerelease.
